title: Projection normalizer + legacy score bridge for embeddings
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Context: We are seeing subtle but persistent client regressions and surprising score drift in reranking customers after a model bump + quantization changes. Root cause analysis shows two correlated issues: (1) inconsistently applied normalization across model ingestion paths (some models are stored already normalized, others are not); (2) ambiguity between cosine and raw dot semantics in downstream scoring code and client integrations. Both cause correctness and quality regressions for rerank endpoints and also make benchmarking noisy.

Problem: There is no single place in the runtime that guarantees embedding projection invariants (unit norm or documented scale). Clients assume either cosine similarity or raw dot; some rely on legacy unnormalized outputs. Changing either behavior breaks rerankers, similarity search thresholds, and monitoring alerts. We need a predictable server-side behavior that fixes correctness for new models while preserving a safe backward-compatibility path for existing clients and customers who depend on dot-product magnitudes.

Goal: Ship a runtime "projection normalizer" that enforces a deterministic normalization policy and a lightweight "legacy score bridge" compatibility mode. The runtime must: (a) compute and optionally cache vector norms; (b) offer a request-level opt-in/out for score semantics; (c) avoid measurable regressions in p95 token latency for embedding endpoints; (d) provide a clear deprecation plan and tooling for customers to migrate to canonical cosine semantics.
proposed_solution: 1) Add a projection normalizer stage in the embedding ingestion pipeline: compute L2 norm for every emitted vector, attach norm metadata to vector objects and to stored vectors in the embedding store. 2) Default server semantics: when no explicit client mode is set, return embeddings unchanged but include response header 'X-Embed-Score-Modes: dot=legacy;cosine=available' and a small info payload describing mode. 3) Provide score-mode options: 'score_mode=dot' (legacy behavior), 'score_mode=cosine' (server computes cosine by dividing by cached norms during score calculation), 'score_mode=cosine_normalize_on_return' (server returns normalized vectors). 4) Implement a lightweight runtime shim so older clients keep previous numeric outputs when they set score_mode=dot. This shim replays legacy quantization rounding and scaling where necessary. 5) Cache norms in the KV cache keyed by (model, vector_id) to avoid recomputing norms for common vectors. 6) Add metric and alerting hooks to detect drift in NDCG/precision for a flagged client prompt set.
design_decisions: Compute norms in float32 for stability; store compressed norm (float16) in KV to cut memory footprint.
Prefer server-side cosine computation over requiring all clients to fetch normalized vectors to reduce client work and bandwidth.
Do not change default numeric outputs for existing customers without opt-in; default is legacy-compatible unless customer migrates.
Expose explicit request parameter and response header for transparency rather than hidden heuristics.
Cache norms with TTL tuned per workload (default 24h) and provide per-model override for heavy-change models.
Keep the quantization-aware shim as a temporary bridge (3-month deprecation) and log usage for sunset planning.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit tests -> PR to platform (canary flag behind runtime feature gate). 2) Internal canary: enable 'cosine' for small % of internal test customers and Redwood-only traffic for 72h. Monitor NDCG, p95 latency, and memory pressure. 3) Customer canaries: opt individual customers via support toggle; pair with migration playbook. 4) Gradual default flip: after 60 days and no regressions on critical metrics, flip docs to recommend cosine and start 90-day deprecation notice for 'dot' default. 5) Final removal: remove legacy shim after 3 months from deprecation if usage < 1% of requests; otherwise extend per-customer plan.
migration_notes:
- Provide a lightweight 'compatibility playground' in Console where customers can test score_mode toggles against their stored vectors and a small prompt set. Link to migration checklist in artifacts.
- For customers using serverless embedding store, run an automated audit that compares stored vector norms vs expected; report potential breakage candidates.
- Create a migration script that can bulk-normalize stored vectors for customers who opt into 'normalize_on_return'.
- Communicate breaking threshold changes to PS and include recommended threshold adjustments (example thresholds for cosine vs dot).
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests covering norm computation, storage, and cache invalidation (100% CI pass).
Integration tests verifying parity of legacy numeric outputs when score_mode=dot for 95% of canonical testcases.
E2E rerank quality on sample corpora: NDCG@10 delta within +/-0.5% when comparing legacy dot vs server cosine for a baseline model (unless model intentionally changes).
Latency: p95 for embed+rerank flow increases no more than 5% in canary; memory pressure increase tolerable (documented).
Console feature toggle + playground available and accessible to design/PM/SEs.
qa_plan:
- Run nightly e2e job that computes NDCG and recall on 4 representative corpora (search, faq, paraphrase, product-match) comparing legacy dot to cosine variants.
- Load test embeddings endpoint with mixed score_mode flags to validate caching behavior and observe cache hit ratio.
- Fuzz tests for malformed score_mode values.
- Manual regression review with DevRel and a sample of customers flagged as high-risk.
- Post-rollout 7-day burn alerting: if any monitored customer's rerank NDCG drops >2% or p95 latency increases >10%, automatically rollback for that customer.
metrics: dashboard: Rerank - NDCG by customer cohort
dashboard: Embedding store - norm cache hit ratio
alert: Regression detector for NDCG drift > 2%
